A gentle evening blue-grey light settles over the rows of upright sugarcane, a farmhouse window's warm glow just visible beyond the field's edge, a plain wooden counter and hand-cranked juice press waiting beside a neat stack of empty glass jars at the row's end.

Thin ground mist drifts through the lower half of the cane rows on a humid misty morning, dew gathered in fine drops along every blade-like leaf overhead, a half-full woven basket and a curved cutting knife resting against the low woven fence at the field's boundary.

A misty morning settles low between the rows of golden-green sugarcane, thin ground mist drifting around the jointed stalks, dew beaded in fine drops along every long blade-like leaf, the far fence line just visible through the soft grey-green haze.

The well-worn dirt path between two rows of tall segmented cane glistens faintly under a flat overcast sky, the even grey-white light falling shadowless across the upright stalks and their fanned leaves, a woven basket sitting half-full at the near row's end.

Silvery moonlight washes across the field in a clean, pale sheet, catching the waxy upper surface of the long leaf blades high on each stalk, the rows standing upright and still, a cart loaded with neatly stacked cut cane lengths resting beside the low wooden fence.

A gentle warm rain falls soft and steady across the field at dusk, darkening the jointed cane stalks to a deep green-grey, water beading and running off the broad leaf blades overhead, a curved cane-cutting knife resting dry against a low fence post under the eave of the row's end.

The far edge of the field appears clearly under a flat overcast midday sky, three or four straight rows of tall segmented cane running toward a low woven boundary fence, a wheelbarrow stacked with freshly cut cane lengths parked squarely at the end of the nearest row.
